discovery: Experimental demonstration of anyonic braiding statistics in fractional quantum Hall systems

nominees.name: Gwendal Fève
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire de Physique de l'Ecole Normale Supérieure, Paris, France

subfield: Condensed matter physics - topological quantum matter
motivation: Fractional statistics, where exchanging two particles produces a phase that is neither boson-like nor fermion-like, was predicted almost fifty years ago as a possibility unique to two dimensions. It underlies our understanding of topological order and topological quantum computation. For decades it went unobserved. In 2020 two complementary experiments settled the question. Fève and collaborators built an anyon collider: cross-correlations of currents colliding at a quantum point contact revealed the braiding phase of Laughlin quasiparticles at filling 1/3, as Rosenow and co-workers had predicted theoretically. Manfra's group engineered ultra-clean GaAs heterostructures and Fabry-Pérot interferometers that suppress Coulomb effects, and they observed discrete phase slips that directly measure the anyonic braiding phase. Later work has extended both methods to other filling fractions. Together these results turned anyons from a theoretical construct into an established property of matter.
